dinners.name: Chilli & Ginger Salmon with Basmati Rice & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, honey, ginger, chilli flakes, garlic and sesame oil together in a small bowl.

Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, pour the glaze over, and cook for a further 3 minutes, spooning the glaze over the fish as it cooks.
While the salmon finishes, steam the pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Plate up rice and pak choi, lay the salmon on top and spoon over any remaining glaze. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: Defrost the fillet in the fridge the night before and pat it dry before it goes in the pan. The ginger and chilli make this a fresher, lighter dish than the miso salmon.

dinners.name: Courgette & Red Lentil Curry with Basmati Rice
method: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, ginger, paprika, mixed herbs, chilli flakes, and garlic powder and cook for 1 more minute.
Add lentils, tinned tomatoes, and stock. Stir well, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Add courgette and cook for a further 10 minutes until lentils are soft and courgette is tender. Season with salt.
While curry finishes, cook rice according to packet instructions (cook fresh each night, 100g per serving).
Serve curry over rice.
dinners.tip: Store the second portion in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of water to loosen.

dinners.name: Crispy Hoisin Cauliflower Bowl with Quinoa & Edamame
method: Preheat oven to 230°C (210°C fan) with a baking tray inside so it heats up.
Toss cauliflower with sunflower oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Spread on the hot tray in a single layer and roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Rinse quinoa, then cook in 120ml water with a pinch of salt: bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 12 minutes. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Boil the edamame from frozen for 4 minutes, then drain.
Mix hoisin, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a bowl. Toss the roasted cauliflower in the sauce and return to the oven for 3–4 minutes to glaze.
Serve the quinoa topped with edamame and the glazed cauliflower. Scatter sesame seeds and chilli flakes over to finish.
dinners.tip: Crowding the tray steams the cauliflower instead of crisping it. Use a single layer, and use two trays if needed.

dinners.name: Crispy Skin Salmon with Soy & Sesame Rice & Tenderstem Broccoli

ingredients.name: lettuce
ingredients.note: to serve, lightly dressed with a few drops of rice vinegar

method: Cook rice according to packet instructions. Once cooked, stir through the soy sauce, sesame oil and rice vinegar. Keep warm.
Pat the salmon skin very dry with kitchen paper and season the skin with salt.

Heat sunflower oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down, pressing gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds so the skin stays flat. Cook for 5–6 minutes without moving it, until the skin is crisp and the flesh is cooked about three-quarters of the way up.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more.
While the salmon cooks, steam or pan-fry the tenderstem broccoli for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve salmon over the sesame rice with the broccoli and lettuce alongside. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: The skin is the whole point here. Dry it thoroughly, don't move the fish while it crisps, and resist the urge to flip early.

dinners.name: Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Spiced Chickpeas & Spinach
method: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until just tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 2 minutes.

Place potatoes on a baking tray. Use the bottom of a glass or mug to firmly smash each one flat. Drizzle with 1.5 tbsp olive oil and season with salt. Roast at 220°C (200°C fan) for 20 minutes until golden and crispy.

While potatoes roast, heat remaining olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add chickpeas, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, paprika and chilli flakes. Toss well and cook for 5–6 minutes until chickpeas are lightly crispy and well coated in spice.
Add spinach to the chickpea pan and stir until wilted.
Serve smashed potatoes topped with spiced chickpeas and spinach.
dinners.tip: The key to crispy smashed potatoes is making sure they're well dried after boiling and generously oiled before roasting. Don't rush the roasting time. The crispier the better.

dinners.name: Cumin & Paprika Chicken with Roasted Courgette & Basmati Rice
method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss courgette rounds with 0.5 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes until golden.
Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chilli flakes, soy sauce and 1 tbsp olive oil in a bowl. Coat chicken thighs well.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
Rest chicken for 2 minutes then serve over rice with roasted courgette alongside.
dinners.tip: Get the courgette in the oven first. It takes the longest and is easy to forget about once the chicken is in the pan.

dinners.name: Cumin Spiced Chicken with Crispy Roasted Potatoes & Basmati Rice
method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss potato chunks with 0.5 tbsp olive oil, 0.5 tsp cumin, and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes until golden and crispy, turning halfway.
Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix remaining cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chilli flakes, soy sauce, and 1 tbsp olive oil in a bowl. Coat chicken thighs well.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
Rest chicken for 2 minutes then serve over rice with crispy potatoes alongside.
dinners.tip: Get the potatoes in first — they take the longest. Don't turn them too early or they'll stick to the tray; wait until they release naturally.

dinners.name: Garam Masala Chickpea Curry with Basmati Rice

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: for Monday; cook fresh for Tuesday

method: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 more minute.
Add tomato puree, garam masala, cumin, turmeric and chilli flakes. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas and chopped tomatoes with 100ml water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Lightly crush a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken it.
Season with salt. Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Toss the chopped tomato and red onion with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve half the curry over rice, topped with the tomato and onion mix. Cool the second portion quickly and store in an airtight container for the next day.
dinners.tip: Chill the second portion within an hour. The spices deepen overnight, so the second portion will taste even better. Make the tomato topping fresh each time.
dinners.boost: stir 75g red lentils into the curry with the tomatoes (add a splash of extra water and simmer for 20 minutes), and serve over quinoa instead of rice. This takes each portion to roughly 28g.

dinners.name: Garam Masala Lentil & Spinach Daal with Crispy Roasted Potatoes

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: grated; or pinch of ground ginger

ingredients.name: chopped tomatoes
ingredients.note: freeze or use the rest in another meal

method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss potato chunks with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, and salt. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25 minutes until golden and crispy, turning halfway.

While potatoes roast, heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, ground coriander, and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add lentils, tomatoes, and stock. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer for 15–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft.
Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Stir spinach into the dal until wilted. Season with salt.
Serve dal over rice with crispy potatoes alongside.
dinners.tip: The potatoes are done when they're golden and crispy on the outside — resist the urge to turn them too early or they'll stick to the tray.

dinners.name: Gochujang & Sesame Chicken with Quinoa, Wilted Spinach & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Rinse quinoa and cook in 180ml of water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Mix gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and garlic together in a bowl. Add chicken thighs and coat well.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
Remove chicken and rest. Add spinach to the same pan and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
While chicken rests, steam pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve chicken over quinoa with spinach and pak choi alongside. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: Gochujang has a good kick — reduce to 1 tbsp and add extra honey if you want less heat.

dinners.name: Gochujang Chicken with Basmati Rice & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and garlic together in a bowl. Add the chicken thighs and coat well.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
While the chicken rests, steam the pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve the chicken over rice with pak choi alongside. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: Gochujang has a good kick. Reduce to 1 tbsp and add extra honey if you want less heat.

dinners.name: Gochujang Chicken with Brown Rice & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook brown rice according to packet instructions (~25 minutes — start first).
Mix gochujang, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and garlic together in a bowl. Add chicken thighs and coat well.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
While chicken rests, steam pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve chicken over rice with pak choi alongside. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: Gochujang has a good kick — if you want less heat, reduce to 1 tbsp and add a little extra honey to balance.

dinners.name: Honey Garlic Chicken with Basmati Rice & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, honey and garlic in a bowl. Add the chicken thighs and coat well.
Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and sticky. Pour the remaining glaze over in the last 2 minutes.
While the chicken rests, steam the pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Whisk rice vinegar and honey together and toss through the lettuce and tomato.
Serve chicken over rice with pak choi and salad alongside.
dinners.tip: Watch the heat once the honey goes in. Medium-high is fine, but the glaze goes from sticky to burnt quickly in the last 2 minutes.

dinners.name: Honey Garlic Chicken with Basmati Rice & Wilted Spinach
method: Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, honey, and garlic together in a small bowl.

Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken thighs for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through. Pour the glaze over and cook for a further 2 minutes, turning to coat. Add butter in the last minute for extra richness.
Remove chicken from the pan and rest. Add spinach to the same pan and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Serve chicken over rice with spinach alongside.
dinners.tip: The honey will catch quickly once added — keep the heat at medium and keep an eye on it.

dinners.name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Soy & Sesame Rice & Tenderstem Broccoli
method: Cook rice according to packet instructions. Once cooked, stir through 0.5 tbsp soy sauce, sesame oil and rice vinegar. Keep warm.
Mix miso paste, remaining soy sauce, honey and garlic together in a small bowl. Spread generously over the salmon fillet.

Heat a pan over medium heat with a small drizzle of oil. Place the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes. Flip and cook for a further 2–3 minutes. The miso glaze will caramelise, so watch it closely as it can catch quickly.
While the salmon finishes, steam or pan-fry the tenderstem broccoli for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve the salmon over sesame rice with broccoli alongside. Scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: Your miso is darker and saltier than white miso, so 1 tbsp with the extra honey keeps it balanced. Keep the heat at medium once you flip. The caramelised edges are the best bit.

dinners.name: Paprika Chicken with Roasted Courgette & Quinoa
method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss courgette rounds with 0.5 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes until golden.
Rinse quinoa, then cook in 120ml water with a pinch of salt: bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 12 minutes. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Mix paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chilli flakes, soy sauce and 1 tbsp olive oil in a bowl. Coat the chicken thighs well.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly crispy. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame oil together and toss through the lettuce and tomato.
Rest chicken for 2 minutes, then serve over quinoa with the courgette and salad alongside.
dinners.tip: Get the courgette in the oven first. It takes the longest, and the same trick makes it nicely golden at the edges.

dinners.name: Quinoa & Roasted Veg Bowl
method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss courgette, pepper, and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, paprika, mixed herbs, garlic powder, and salt on a baking tray. Spread out in a single layer.
Roast for 20–25 minutes until tender and slightly charred at the edges.
While veg roasts, rinse quinoa and cook in 180ml of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Spoon quinoa into a bowl and top with roasted veg.
dinners.tip: Feel free to swap in any veg you have going. Mushrooms, red onion, or aubergine all work well here.
dinners.boost: Add a tin of drained chickpeas to the roasting tray (adds ~10g and gets nicely crispy).

dinners.name: Quinoa & Roasted Veg Bowl with Salmon
method: Preheat oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss courgette, pepper, and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, paprika, mixed herbs, garlic powder, and salt on a baking tray. Spread out in a single layer and roast for 20–25 minutes.
While veg roasts, rinse quinoa and cook in 180ml of water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Mix soy sauce and honey in a small bowl. Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes, flip, pour over the glaze and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Spoon quinoa into a bowl, top with roasted veg and flake the salmon over the top.

dinners.name: Red Lentil Dal with Basmati Rice
method: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic, paprika, mixed herbs, and chilli flakes and cook for 1 more minute.
Add lentils, tinned tomatoes, and stock. Stir well, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft and the dal has thickened.
Season with salt. Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Serve dal over rice.
dinners.tip: This makes 2 portions — have the second as lunch the next day or dinner on Monday if needed.

dinners.name: Soy & Sesame Glazed Salmon with Rice & Tenderstem Broccoli

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: grated; or pinch of ground ginger

method: Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, garlic, and ginger together in a small bowl.

Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, pour the glaze over, and cook for a further 3 minutes, spooning the glaze over the fish as it cooks.
While salmon finishes, steam or pan-fry tenderstem broccoli for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Plate up rice and broccoli, lay salmon on top, spoon over any remaining glaze, and scatter sesame seeds over to finish.
dinners.tip: The sesame oil adds a lovely nutty depth — don't be tempted to swap it for olive oil here as it really makes the dish.

dinners.name: Soy-Glazed Chicken with Brown Rice & Tenderstem Broccoli
method: Cook the brown rice according to packet instructions. Start it first, as it takes longest.
Mix soy sauce, honey, garlic powder, paprika, chilli flakes and olive oil in a bowl. Coat the chicken thighs well.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and crisp at the edges. Pour any remaining glaze over in the last 2 minutes.
While the chicken rests for 2 minutes, steam the tenderstem broccoli for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the broccoli alongside.
dinners.tip: Brown rice is the slow part on a weeknight, so put it on before you do anything else.

dinners.name: Soy-Glazed Chicken with Courgette & Quinoa
method: Rinse quinoa and cook in 180ml of water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
Mix soy sauce, garlic powder, paprika, and chilli flakes in a bowl. Add chicken thighs and coat well.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
Remove chicken and rest. Add courgette slices to the same pan and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Slice chicken and serve over quinoa with courgette alongside.
dinners.tip: Cooking the courgette in the same pan picks up all the leftover spiced juices — don't wipe it clean between steps.

dinners.name: Spiced Chickpea & Tomato Pasta
method: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, paprika, mixed herbs, and chilli flakes and cook for 1 more minute.
Add tinned tomatoes, stock, and chickpeas. Stir well and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
While the sauce simmers, cook pasta according to packet instructions. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
Stir pasta through the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed. Season with salt.
dinners.tip: Store the second portion in an airtight container in the fridge and reheat with a splash of water.

dinners.name: Spiced Coconut Lentil Dal with Basmati Rice
method: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 more minute.
Add cumin, turmeric, garam masala, ground coriander, and chilli flakes. Stir well and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add lentils, tinned tomatoes, and coconut milk. Stir well, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are completely soft and the dal has thickened to a creamy consistency. Add a splash of water if it thickens too quickly.
Season with salt. Cook rice fresh each night (100g per serving).
Serve dal over rice.
dinners.tip: Store the second portion in an airtight container in the fridge. The coconut flavour deepens overnight so Friday's portion will taste even better.

dinners.name: Spiced Lamb Meatballs with Basmati Rice & Pan-Fried Courgette
method: Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix minced lamb with garlic, paprika, mixed herbs, chilli flakes, onion powder, garlic powder, and salt. Shape into small meatballs, about the size of a golf ball (makes around 8–10).
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook meatballs for 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over and cooked through.
Remove meatballs and rest. Add courgette slices to the same pan and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until golden, picking up the lamb juices.
Serve meatballs and courgette over rice.
dinners.tip: Don't overcrowd the pan with the meatballs — cook in batches if needed to get a good colour on them rather than steaming.

dinners.name: Sticky Hoisin Pork Belly with Basmati Rice, Stir-Fried Tenderstem Broccoli & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook basmati rice according to packet instructions.
Mix hoisin sauce, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, and chilli flakes together in a bowl. Add pork belly slices and coat well.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook pork belly slices for 4–5 minutes per side until caramelised and cooked through. Pour any remaining marinade over in the last 2 minutes.
While pork rests, stir-fry tenderstem broccoli in the same pan with sliced garlic for 3–4 minutes until tender with a little char.
Steam pak choi in a separate pan or steamer for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Serve pork belly over rice with broccoli and pak choi alongside.
dinners.tip: Don't rush the pork — letting it caramelise properly in the pan is what makes this dish impressive. If the marinade starts catching too quickly, add a small splash of water to the pan.

dinners.name: Teriyaki Salmon with Basmati Rice & Steamed Pak Choi
method: Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, honey and garlic together in a small bowl.

Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, pour the teriyaki mix over, and cook for a further 3 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish as it thickens.
While the salmon finishes, steam the pak choi for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Toss the sliced tomato with sesame oil, rice vinegar and sesame seeds.
Plate up rice and pak choi, lay the salmon on top and spoon over any remaining sauce. Serve with the tomato salad.
dinners.tip: Defrost the fillet in the fridge the night before so the skin crisps properly. Pat it dry before it goes in the pan.

dinners.name: Teriyaki Salmon with Rice & Wilted Spinach with Garlic
method: Cook rice according to packet instructions.
Mix soy sauce, honey, and minced garlic together in a small bowl.

Melt butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, pour the glaze over, and cook for a further 3 minutes, spooning the glaze over the fish as it cooks.
Remove salmon. Add sliced garlic to the same pan and cook for 30 seconds, then add spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Plate up rice, lay salmon on top, and serve spinach alongside.
